Meeting Date:  September 12, 2024
From:  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Sandra Dolson, Administrative Secretary

Subject
Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

Recommendation
Select one member to serve as Chair and one member to serve as Vice Chair for the term ending
on June 30, 2025.

Background
The Business and Industry Commission consists of seven members including three Business
Representatives, one Council Member, one Employee/Labor Representative, and two Real
Estate Representatives. Members serve four-year terms, for no more than two full consecutive
terms. The current members are as follows:

  Date
  Commissioner  Appointing Category  End of Term
  Appointed
Catherine Browne  Business Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Navdeep (Duncan) Sachdeva  Business Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Brian Bailey  Business Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Melissa Ybarra  Council Member  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028
Hector Morfin  Employee/Labor Representative June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Thomas Condon  Real Estate Representative  June 7, 2022  June 30, 2026
Paul Sablock  Real Estate Representative  June 4, 2024  June 30, 2028

Municipal Code Section 2.52.100.B. requires a Chair and Vice Chair be selected annually from
different appointing categories and prohibits a member from serving as Chair for more than two
(2) consecutive terms.

Chair Sachdeva was selected to serve as Chair on July 14, 2022, and re-selected on August 10,
2023, serving two consecutive terms. Pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section 2.52.100.B,
Commissioner Sachdeva is not eligible to serve another term as Chair. All other Commissioners
are eligible to serve as Chair. The Commission should select a Chair and Vice Chair to serve
through June 30, 2025.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Department:  Public Utilities
Submitted by:  Adriana Ramos, Senior Management Analyst

Subject
Presentation on Vernon Public Utilities Reliability Metrics

Recommendation
No action required by The Commission. This is a presentation only.

Background
Each year, the American Public Power Association (APPA), an organization representing over
2,000 community-owned electric utilities nationwide, recognizes select utilities based on their
electric reliability. Vernon Public Utilities (VPU) was among the 2023 recipients of APPA’s
Certificate of Excellence in Reliability, a nationally recognized annual award. This is the fourth
consecutive year that the APPA has honored VPU for its exceptional electric reliability. The
primary causes of outages in Vernon are metallic balloons, vehicle accidents, and severe
weather. In an effort to maintain/enhance reliability, VPU takes proactive measures to minimize
the effects of these risks, such as installing bird guards and upgrading line voltage. VPU Staff
will provide a presentation to the Business and Industry Commission on their reliability metrics
and notable highlights including:
  ▪ VPU’s achievement as a 3-time Diamond Level Reliable Public Power Provider (RP3)
  ▪ VPU’s rank in top 25 percent of utilities nationwide for low duration of electrical outages
  ▪ VPU’s outage duration and frequency versus national average
  o 2023 VPU average outage duration of 29.69 minutes, compared to national
  average of 148 minutes
  o Average of 0.52 outages per customer, compared to national average of 1.07
  ▪ VPU’s consistent position as a top-quartile utility, surpassing neighboring utilities like
  Southern California Edison and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power
  (LADWP). VPU’s electric system is consistently over 99.99% reliable.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Meeting Date:  September 12, 2024
From:  Robert Sousa, Chief of Police
Department:  Police
Submitted by:  Brandon Gray, Captain

Subject
Presentation on Public Safety Initiatives, Technological Enhancements, and Crime Statistics

Recommendation
No action required by the Commission. This is a presentation only.

Background
Public safety is a key priority for the City. In recent years, the Vernon Police Department (VPD)
has been working to implement modern technologies that enhance our ability to prevent, monitor,
and respond to incidents throughout the City. The use of technology in public safety ensures
efficient and timely responses to emergencies, improves communication between departments,
and offers more robust data decision-making.

VPD staff will provide information to the Business and Industry Commission on recent public
safety developments including:
  1. Crime Statistics and Response Times
  2. Community Policing Efforts
  3. Technology Implementations
  4. Future Technology Initiatives

The City is committed to continuing its investment in cutting-edge technology to enhance public
safety and improve response times. These innovations foster a safer environment and provide
our public safety personnel with the tools they need to serve the community more effectively.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

Attachments
None.

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Fiscal Year 2024-25 Proposed Budget Overview

  Financial Services Administrator Alcaraz presented the report.

  In response to Commission questions, Financial Services Administrator Alcaraz,
  Deputy City Administrator Kimmey, and Assistant General Manager Otto provided
  information on revenue, budget reserves, and fiber optics.

2.  Metro Link Union Station (Link US) Project

  LA Metro staff, Carlos Montez, Deputy Executive Officer, Countywide Planning and
  Development, and Danielle Valentino, Manager, Community Relations provided
  information and an accompanying PowerPoint presentation.

  In response to Commission questions, LA Metro provided information on the Metro Link
  Union Station Link US Project, 49th Street closure, options and outreach efforts and
  feedback from property owners.

  Chair Sachdeva thanked LA Metro and invited public comment.

  Michael Melideo, the owner of Consolidated Fabricators, addressed the traffic impacts
  and safety concerns of the project along Santa Fe and 49th Street. He also mentioned
  the potential impacts on his ability to conduct business at 4600 and 4848 Santa Fe.

  Randy Greenberg of Crystal Art Gallery, requested more follow-up from LA Metro.

  Stephanie Sagaub, property manager of 4811 Hampton requested more information
  from LA Metro on the project and traffic impacts related to the 200 trucks coming into
  the business weekly.

  Marissa Olguin, Vernon Chamber of Commerce, spoke encouraging LA Metro and the
  City to re-evaluate traffic impacts on local businesses and requested more
  collaboration.

  In response to Commission and public questions, LA Metro representatives expressed
  willingness to follow up on the input received and provided information related to the
  timeline of the EIR, the public review and comment period, and willingness to meet with
  stakeholders to address concerns and mitigate impacts to the city.

  The Commission reached a consensus to invite LA Metro to bring the item back for
  further discussion at a Special Meeting with a date to be determined.
